problem: Video-based VLMs for monocular VLN (NaVid, Uni-NaVid) poorly capture 3D geometry and spatial semantics, lack structured long-term scene memory (no pre-exploration or lifelong memory), and cannot adapt to dynamically changing scenes.
motivation: Most robots have only monocular cameras, so monocular VLN with large models is practical, but historical frame representations are inadequate for large-scale, changing 3D environments. Instruction targets are described mostly as object instances and room layouts, so a language-aligned hierarchical 3D representation that updates online should improve localization, exploration and error correction.
key_idea: Build an online, language-aligned patch-instance-zone hierarchical 3D token representation with frustum-culling dynamic updates, and feed it (with rendered panoramic patch tokens) to a 3.8B 3D-VLM that directly predicts low-level navigation actions.
insight: Instance and zone tokens matter: removing both (patch tokens only) drops R2R-CE SR from 52.9 to 45.7 and REVERIE-CE SR from 40.1 to 25.7; removing Subspace Contrastive Learning lowers R2R-CE SR to 50.7, showing that view-bias-robust distillation matters. Structured persistent memory also helps directly: pre-exploration and lifelong memory raise SR to 57.1 / 55.6 and 58.4 combined, which video-frame models cannot exploit.
method: Patch feature points with frustum culling: CLIP-ViT-L/14@336 patch features are back-projected to 3D with depth and pose (storing orientation and region size); points inside the current view frustum that lie in front of observed depth are removed before adding new ones, so moved or removed objects are forgotten.

Dynamic 3D instance encoding: FastSAM 2D masks; a transformer instance encoder with a learnable query aggregates patch features plus positional embeddings; an MLP Merging Discriminator (2D/3D instance features + distance, Top-K nearest) merges into existing 3D instances or creates new ones; instances are re-encoded as patches are culled and deleted when empty.

Language alignment and distillation: instance-text contrastive loss on SceneVerse/g3D-LF 3D-language data, CLIP distillation with Masked Average Pooling targets, and Subspace Contrastive Learning that subtracts the per-view mean feature to remove view bias.

Zone representation: the world is split into uniform cubic zones; a zone encoder aggregates instance features into zone tokens, distilled to whole-view CLIP features and aligned with long text via g3D-LF fine-grained contrastive learning.
Panoramic 3D patch tokens: the g3D-LF generalizable feature field renders 12x48 rays (360° horizontal, 90° vertical) around the agent, giving agent-centric patch features.

3D-VLM action predictor: LLaVA-Phi-3-mini (3.8B) takes patch, instance, zone, instruction and last-4-action tokens with relative-position MLP embeddings, and outputs turn-left/right θ, forward d cm, or stop.

Two-stage navigation training: imitation on GT paths, then DAgger-style exploration and correction with waypoint-predictor deviations; the LLM is fully fine-tuned while the feature field and Dynam3D representation model stay frozen.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-Phi-3-mini 3.8B (fine-tuned) + CLIP-ViT-L/14@336 + FastSAM + g3D-LF feature field + Dynam3D representation model (trained)
setting.training_data: Representation: 5K+ scenes with 2M language annotations (ScanNet, HM3D, MP3D, 3RScan, ARKitScenes, Structured3D; SceneVerse/g3D-LF). Navigation: 4M+ continuous-environment instruction-trajectory pairs from ScaleVLN and NavRAG plus 20K+ human-annotated R2R-CE/REVERIE-CE, sampled 1:1; 100K episodes of imitation and DAgger training.
setting.observation: monocular posed RGB-D (forward-facing), with camera pose
setting.action_space: low-level: turn left/right θ degrees, forward d cm, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (continuous), plus Hello Robot Stretch 3 in the real world
setting.privileged: none for standard results (poses assumed); the pre-exploration and lifelong-memory variants use panoramic images at annotated MP3D viewpoints or memory from earlier episodes

numbers_note: Table splits are labelled 'Val' in the paper; mapped to val-unseen (the ablation caption says 'R2R-CE Val Unseen'). Real-world results (20 trials each): static SR 55 (70 with pre-exploration), dynamic SR 45; not included as they are not on a canonical benchmark.
results: Dynam3D reaches R2R-CE val SR 52.9 / SPL 45.7 and test SR 51.4, beating g3D-LF (47.2) and Uni-NaVid (47.0) by about 5 SR points with a 3.8B model versus 7B. On REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE it gets SR 40.1 and 24.7 versus g3D-LF 34.4 and 21.4 (baselines retrained on the authors' data). Pre-exploration plus lifelong memory lifts R2R-CE SR to 58.4, and real-world SR beats NaVid and g3D-LF.
limitations: Predicts only actions, not target coordinates, so it is less suited to mobile manipulation; it cannot do QA, dialogue or task updates.
Requires posed RGB-D (pose and depth) input, and inference takes about 0.65 s per step on an RTX 4090.
Very heavy training cost (about 8 days plus 9 days on RTX 6000 Ada GPUs); the real-world evaluation is small (20 trials per setting).
